blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
For much of the twentieth century, corporate learning rested on a stable assumption: skills acquired early in a career would remain valuable for decades. That assumption is no longer defensible. Technology cycles have compressed, entire professions are being redefined within a single decade, and skills that were rare three years ago are now table stakes in job descriptions.

What this demands from HR is a fundamental shift: from training as an event to learning as a condition of employment. The real question is not "What courses should we offer this year?" but "How do we build an organisation where continuous learning is structurally inevitable rather than occasionally encouraged?"

It is the organisations that treat reskilling as a strategic capability — backed by real investment, real time and real career protection for those who engage — that pull ahead. Those that treat it as a communication exercise eventually find themselves paying twice: once for the talent they lose, and once for the talent they must rehire at a market premium.

items.q: According to the text, why is the twentieth-century assumption about skills no longer defensible?
options: Because technology cycles have compressed and professions are being redefined within a decade
Because employees change jobs more frequently than before
Because universities no longer teach relevant subjects
Because training budgets have been cut across the sector
items.why: "Technology cycles have compressed, entire professions are being redefined within a single decade."

items.q: How does the text reframe the central question HR should be asking?
options: From which vendor to choose to which platform performs best
From what courses to offer to how to make continuous learning structurally inevitable
From how much to spend to how quickly to certify staff
From who to train first to who to promote next
items.why: "not 'What courses should we offer this year?' but 'How do we build an organisation where continuous learning is structurally inevitable…'"

items.q: What does the text mean when it says such organisations end up "paying twice"?
options: They pay for both training and recruitment consultants
They lose talent and then rehire it at a market premium
They fund two separate learning platforms at once
They compensate staff for lost time and lost bonuses
items.why: "once for the talent they lose, and once for the talent they must rehire at a market premium."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: A one-off training campaign is enough to future-proof a workforce
Reskilling deserves genuine investment and time
Career protection encourages employees to engage in learning
Skills can lose their scarcity value within a few years
items.why: Inferência: o texto opõe 'training as an event' a 'learning as a condition' — uma campanha pontual é exatamente o que ele critica.

items.q: The phrase "learning as a condition of employment" most strongly suggests that…
options: learning should be optional and self-directed
continuous learning becomes intrinsic to the job, not an occasional add-on
employees who refuse training should be dismissed
items.why: Inferência: 'condition of employment' significa parte estrutural do trabalho, não um evento avulso.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Harry defendendo o investimento em requalificação diante do comitê. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Let me be direct about what I'm asking the committee to approve. This isn't a training line item — it's a three-year reskilling investment for a department whose technical base is going obsolete faster than any of us expected.

What I want you to hear is the maths of doing nothing. If we let this team's skills lapse, we don't just lose capability — we lose the people, because good engineers read the writing on the wall and leave. Then we rehire at a market premium, twelve to eighteen months later, for skills we could have built in-house at a fraction of the cost.

So the proposal has three non-negotiables. Real time — protected hours, not evenings and weekends. Real money — a proper budget, not what's left over. And career protection, so that anyone who commits to reskilling knows their role is safe while they learn.

What I'm not proposing is a communication exercise. We've all sat through the all-staff email that calls itself a strategy. This is the opposite: fewer promises, more structure. Get those three right, and continuous learning stops being something we encourage and becomes something the organisation simply does.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: How does Harry describe the proposal he is asking the committee to approve?
options: A three-year reskilling investment for a department going obsolete
A recruitment drive for new engineers
items.why: "it's a three-year reskilling investment for a department whose technical base is going obsolete."

items.q: What are the three non-negotiables in Harry's proposal?
options: Real time, real money and career protection
New tools, new managers and new metrics
Fewer meetings, more emails and clearer goals
items.why: "Real time… Real money… And career protection."

items.q: What does Harry mean by "the maths of doing nothing"?
options: The cost of losing people and rehiring their skills at a premium
The number of courses the team would need to complete
The savings gained by cancelling the programme
The time required to calculate the budget
items.why: Inferência: ele detalha que a inação leva a perder pessoas e recontratar caro — esse é o custo de não agir.

items.q: When Harry says "good engineers read the writing on the wall and leave," he implies that…
options: engineers dislike change and resist new tools
skilled people recognise a declining situation early and exit before it worsens
the department has poor internal communication
the wall displays official company notices
items.why: Inferência: 'read the writing on the wall' = perceber os sinais de declínio; os melhores saem antes.

items.q: What contrast does Harry draw at the end of his pitch?
options: Between his plan and a mere communication exercise
items.why: "What I'm not proposing is a communication exercise… This is the opposite: fewer promises, more structure."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Data-annotation was a niche skill in 2021; today it is simply table stakes for the role." Here table stakes means…
options: the minimum requirement just to be considered
items.why: Table stakes = requisito mínimo, o básico para entrar no jogo.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "We need to ___ the whole support team on the new platform before the migration."
items.why: To reskill = requalificar — ensinar novas competências a quem já está na equipe.

items.q: "A clear skills framework lets us map each role to the capabilities it actually requires." A skills framework is…
options: a structured map of the competencies a role or organisation needs
a list of approved training vendors
items.why: Skills framework = framework de competências: o mapa estruturado das habilidades por papel.

items.q: "The programme isn't a perk; it's about capability building across the function." This refers to…
options: systematically developing the organisation's ability to do new things
hiring external consultants for a project
items.why: Capability building = construção de capacidades — desenvolver de forma sistemática o que a organização sabe fazer.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Because technology cycles have ___, a skill can lose its value in under three years."
items.why: To compress = comprimir; os ciclos ficaram mais curtos, encurtando a vida útil das habilidades.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem em reuniões sobre L&D e futuro do trabalho. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The board still has to sign off on the reskilling budget." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We'll roll out the learning platform team by team over the next quarter." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "Finance pushed back on the protected-hours clause." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "Everyone endorsed the plan, but leadership never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim aquilo que foi combinado.

items.q: "A single lunch-and-learn won't move the needle on our skills gap." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.
